from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Binary digits represent powers of two.", "Example: 13 is 8 plus 4 plus 1.", "In binary, 13 becomes 1101."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Bits", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Animation Objects ---
        bit0 = Text("0", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        bit1 = Text("1", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(bit0, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(bit1, "B4")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Binary digits represent powers of two.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(bit0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Example: 13 is 8 plus 4 plus 1.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(bit0.animate.set_color("#FFD700").become(bit1))
        self.play(FadeIn(bit1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # In binary, 13 becomes 1101.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi: Rules of the Game", [
            "Three rods hold disks of different sizes.",
            "Rule: Move one disk at a time.",
            "Rule: No larger disk on a smaller one."
        ])
        
        # Define assets
        rods = VGroup(*[Line(DOWN, UP) for _ in range(3)]).set_color(WHITE)
        disks = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(height=0.3, width=w, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=1) 
            for w in [1.5, 1.2, 0.9]
        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.05)
        
        # Draw rods
        self.place_at_grid(rods[0], 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(rods[1], 'E4')
        self.place_at_grid(rods[2], 'E6')
        self.add(rods)
        
        # Draw disks on first rod
        for i, disk in enumerate(disks):
            disk.move_to(self.grid['E2'] + DOWN * (0.15 + i * 0.15))
        self.add(disks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(disks[0].animate.move_to(self.grid['E4'] + DOWN * 0.45))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Disk moves mirror binary counting patterns.",
            "Binary steps determine which disk moves.",
            "Example: Step 1 moves disk 1.",
            "Step 2 moves disk 2.",
            "Step 3 moves disk 1 again."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Binary Connection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        binary_label = Text("001", color="#00FF00", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_label, "B3")
        
        disk = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(disk, "E3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_label), FadeIn(disk))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        binary_label2 = Text("010", color="#00FFFF", font_size=40).move_to(binary_label.get_center())
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(binary_label, binary_label2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        disk_move = disk.copy()
        self.play(disk_move.animate.shift(UP * 1.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        binary_label3 = Text("011", color="#FFFF00", font_size=40).move_to(binary_label2.get_center())
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(binary_label2, binary_label3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeOut(binary_label3), FadeOut(disk), FadeOut(disk_move))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one.",
            "Complexity grows exponentially with more disks.",
            "This puzzle demonstrates recursive algorithmic logic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application and Complexity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#00FFFF", "#FF00FF", "#FFFF00"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualize the growth 2^n - 1
        formula = MathTex(r"2^n - 1", font_size=40).set_color(colors[0])
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show growth curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 32, 8], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 2**x - 1, color=colors[1])
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(graph, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight logic
        tag = Text("RECURSION", font_size=30, color=colors[2])
        self.place_at_grid(tag, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(tag, shift=UP))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Binary counting defines the Hanoi solution.", 
                         "Recursive problems often share this structure.", 
                         "Simple binary logic hides deep complexity."]
        
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Hidden Logic", lecture_lines)
        
        # Add visual elements
        key_concepts = VGroup(
            Text("Bits", color=BLUE),
            Text("Hanoi", color=GREEN),
            Text("Binary", color=YELLOW),
            Text("Complexity", color=RED)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_at_grid(key_concepts, 'A1', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Binary counting defines the Hanoi solution.
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(key_concepts[0]), FadeIn(key_concepts[1]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Recursive problems often share this structure.
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(key_concepts[2]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Simple binary logic hides deep complexity.
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(FadeIn(key_concepts[3]))
        
        summary = Text("Logic is everywhere", font_size=40, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(summary, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Hidden Logic
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
sections.content: Briefly introduce the binary system (base-2). Explain how binary digits (0 and 1) represent positions as powers of 2. Emphasize that any decimal number can be expressed as a unique combination of these powers.
sections.example: Visualizing '13' in binary: 8+4+0+1 = 1101₂. Use a row of 4 light bulbs where 'On' = 1 and 'Off' = 0.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi: Rules of the Game
sections.content: Present the puzzle: Three rods, N disks of different sizes. Rules: 1) Move one disk at a time, 2) Never place a larger disk on a smaller one. Define the goal as moving the entire stack from Rod A to Rod C.
sections.example: An animation of 3 disks (Small, Medium, Large) moving from left to right, highlighting the 'impossible' illegal moves.

sections.title: The Binary Connection
sections.content: Reveal the magic: The disk movement sequence corresponds directly to binary counting. If you count in binary (001, 010, 011, 100...), the disk that moves at step 'n' corresponds to the position of the rightmost '1' in the binary representation of 'n'.
sections.example: For 3 disks: Step 1 (001) moves Disk 1; Step 2 (010) moves Disk 2; Step 3 (011) moves Disk 1; Step 4 (100) moves Disk 3.

sections.title: Application and Complexity
sections.content: Connect the math to the physical puzzle: The minimum number of moves required is 2^n - 1. Explain why this grows exponentially, making the puzzle a classic example of recursion and algorithmic complexity.
sections.example: A 'Robot Snail' moving disks according to the binary clock. If n=10, the snail must perform 1,023 steps, showing how binary logic dictates the time taken.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.content: Summarize how binary is not just for computers but is the underlying rhythm of recursive problems. Reiterate that complex puzzles are often just simple binary counting in disguise.
sections.example: A final visual showing the 'Binary Tree' structure of the moves mapping onto the rods of the Hanoi puzzle.
